# Painted lion-tailed monkey

Created with built-in image generation. First input: original generated companion. Second input: user-provided animal illustration reference sheet. Transparent alpha preserved. Rendered mirrored in the website at the existing small size; tail curls tightly against the body. Original asset retained.

## Prompt

Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: transparent illustrated lion-tailed macaque for a small rope-hanging website companion.
Image 1: edit target, existing monkey cutout and precise grip placement.
Image 2: reference for illustration technique ONLY.
Redraw Image 1 in a charming painterly animal-book illustration style inspired by Image 2: simplified chunky irregular geometric shapes, visible dry gouache texture, soft paper grain inside shapes, fine scratchy pencil accents, expressive small eyes, confidently drawn silhouette. It must clearly read as an illustration rather than photographic fur. Do not copy the animals from Image 2.
Keep the identifiable lion-tailed macaque: charcoal-black body, broad silver-grey mane/beard, dark muzzle, warm amber eyes, and tuft at the tail tip. Keep its original pose with both gripping hands on the RIGHT of the picture, aligned vertically at approximately x=70.3%, with upper grip y=7% and lower grip y=28.9%. Keep subject scale and hand positions relative to the square canvas like Image 1; the website mirrors it. No rope drawn: website renders its own textured rope behind its gripping hands.
Change the tail so it curls closely along the monkey's outer hip and thigh, tucked in a compact hook shape, with the tuft close to the lower body, NOT sweeping far left or far below the feet. Draw complete legs and feet. Make all shape interiors opaque with painted texture, clean transparent space outside.
Keep genuinely transparent alpha background, original square aspect ratio and room around the silhouette. No panel, text, watermark, logos, trees, rope, ground, or other creatures.
